intro.text: A Vorin woman's left hand, kept covered for modesty. Her right hand is her freehand.

description.text: Darkeyed women, who need both hands for work, often wear a glove instead, as do Thaylen women. Gloves are thought less modest than sleeves.
Prostitutes may wear fingerless gloves or leave the safehand bare to show what they are.

Women in the Vorin nations cover the safehand from about twelve, a rite of passage. It is hidden whenever possible, touching someone with it is intimate and only for family, and showing it deliberately is usually reserved for a partner.

Upper-class women cover it with the long sleeve of a havah, thin enough to grip through. The sleeve often holds a safepouch for personal objects, and opening another woman's safepouch is extremely rude.

items.text: Some singers who served Vorin masters as slaves kept covering their safehands after they were freed.
During the True Desolation the custom seemed to matter less to some high-ranking women. Jasnah kept it only because it was proper, and Navani took to wearing a glove, finding the sleeve a burden.
